subject: Medisphere GCP SKU bundle & reseller pass-through (pricing clarification)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medisphere.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP bundle + reseller margin question

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for a GCP marketplace purchase that will flow through our preferred reseller (CloudResell). A couple of constraints from procurement:

- They'd prefer a single-line private offer on the marketplace (one SKU) rather than multiple individual SKUs.
- The reseller needs a 15% net margin on the deal (their business requirement).
- We want a 12-month committed nodehour equivalent but with the ability to burst (metered) above commit.

Can Redwood present a bundled SKU (bundle = baseline nodehours + burst credits) and still allow CloudResell to show a 15% margin without breaking the marketplace billing flow? Also: any implications for list price visibility and distributor pass-through?

I've attached our SOW template for context (SOW-draft.pdf). We're hoping to finalize commercials within two weeks.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Procurement
Medisphere Health
Attachment(s): SOW-draft.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP bundle + reseller margin question

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear brief and the SOW. Looping in Ben and Connor from Partner Ops so we can coordinate channel routing. A few clarifying questions before we put formal numbers together: 

1) Commit shape: is the commit a flat annual nodehour number (e.g., 5M nodehours/year) or do you want monthly phasing? We can model both.
2) Burst profile: rough expectation for peak usage (x% over commit) so we can size burst credits.
3) Reseller flow: when you say 15% net margin, do you expect that to be visible on the marketplace invoice (line item for reseller fee) or handled outside (reseller invoices Medisphere separately)?

High-level options we typically propose for this ask (I attached a short workbook):
- Option A — Single-bundle SKU (GCP-M1-BUNDLE): one marketplace SKU representing baseline commit + burst credits. Redwood lists the SKU price; CloudResell is set as a reseller in GCP marketplace. We can configure a 15% partner uplift and a back-end passback so the partner receives net margin.
- Option B — Two-line presentation (cleaner visibility): list baseline as one SKU and burst as a metered SKU. This makes invoicing and partner margin math explicit but is not the single-line experience you requested.

I've attached an initial pricing workbook (medisphere-pricing-options.xlsx). If you can confirm the three points above I'll convert Option A into a draft private offer and an indicative quote.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): medisphere-pricing-options.xlsx

Naomi / team — quick partner ops note:

- We can do Option A (single bundled SKU) but need CloudResell to be configured as an authorized reseller/partner in GCP. That allows the marketplace to route revenue and enables the reseller to claim their margin via the distributor pass-through.
- For the 15% margin target: typical approach is to bake that into the partner uplift field (a percentage applied to the net revenue waterfall). On Redwood's side we track net rev allocation per-entity so internal reporting and revenue recognition are clean.
- Tax & invoicing: GCP marketplace generally invoices the buyer (Medisphere). Reseller margin is either shown as a pass-through on the marketplace invoice (requires distributor involvement) or handled off-invoice via a reseller credit note. The former is cleaner for procurement but requires early distributor setup.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Samir, share the procurement contact and any billing constraints (PO rules / single-invoice must-haves).
2) Connor will draft the marketplace config and mapping for a single SKU (bundle -> GCP-M1-BUNDLE).
3) Naomi to issue an indicative quote and outline the reseller passback mechanics.

Ben Carter
Director, Partner GTM | Redwood Inference

Thanks — procurement is Procurement <procurement@medisphere.ai> (cc'd on this reply). A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the workbook: 

- We will give you monthly phasing (we prefer to show commit by month).
- Burst expectation is ~30% peak above baseline for Q4 lift.
- The reseller needs the 15% margin to be reflected in the commercials we sign (Medisphere doesn't want to manage separate post-invoice credits if we can avoid it).

Procurement also attached our purchasing guidelines for public cloud marketplace deals (procurement-guidelines.pdf). A couple of items in there that matter to you: single invoice for our finance team, clear list price visibility for audits, and a short payment window (Net 30).

Question: can Redwood issue a private offer where the list price is visible to us but the partner uplift is configured on the back-end so the invoice still shows a single line and the reseller receives their 15% without Medisphere having to process a second invoice?

Best,

Hi Samir / Procurement team —

Appreciate the guidance and the procurement doc. Short answer: yes, we can produce the single-line private offer experience you want while enabling a 15% reseller margin to be delivered to CloudResell, provided we set up the partner routing correctly with the distributor. Outline of the approach and next steps below: 

Summary of proposed commercial construct (high-level)
- SKU: GCP-M1-BUNDLE (single-line bundle on GCP marketplace)
- List price: we will show a single-line list price on the marketplace and the private-offer page for Medisphere (transparent for audits).
- Net allocation: Redwood will configure a 15% reseller uplift to flow to CloudResell via distributor pass-through (no separate invoice required from Medisphere).
- Commit shape: we will model monthly commit phasing you provide; burst credits will be metered at the published overage rate.
- Billing: Medisphere receives one invoice from GCP marketplace (Net 30). Distributor handles partner settlement to CloudResell.

Attachments included: final-quote-medisphere-20270829.pdf (indicative pricing & commit table).

Open items / timing
1) Procurement: confirm PO reference format and whether you need the reseller name printed on the invoice.
2) Samir: send monthly phasing numbers and final legal approver for the private offer signature.
3) Ben/Connor/Vanessa: we'll need distributor setup (CloudResell) and to confirm whether the reseller will be an authorized re-seller or a sub-distributor.

If that all looks good I will: (a) create the private offer draft in GCP marketplace, (b) produce a HubSpot deal (MED-2027-043) and a DocuSign envelope for the MSA amendment, and (c) circulate the final quote. Goal: private-offer draft in 3 business days assuming we get the phasing.

Thanks — talk soon.

Naomi Feldman
